title: bug: chat_wait's backlog drain returns the whole tail of every unread channel, so one message routed to a seat in an unwatched channel delivers every other seat's messages there too, and the channels filter ("routed mentions still arrive from any channel") is not honored
description:
Found by the governor at 18:20Z on 2026-11-03, live on its own seat. Code read at moe/work-2026-10-24 c99801aa.

PROBLEM:
- The live wake path filters correctly. ChatWaiter.isRelevant (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatWait.ts:169-183) admits a message from a watched channel, or one whose routingTargets include the caller (:179). With no filter, it admits routed messages and humans only (:183).
- The backlog drain does not. backlogChannelIds (packages/moe-daemon/src/util/chatBacklog.ts:125) scans the filter's channels PLUS every channel with an unread count, on the assumption that "Unread channels are already mention-routed (including groups)" (:133). With no filter it scans the unread channels.
- collectChatBacklog (:153) then returns EVERY message after the caller's cursor in each scanned channel (:196 pushes everything not sent by the caller). The doc comment at :147 says so: "No mention/human relevance filter is applied".
- So one routed message in an unwatched channel marks it unread, and the next drain (entry drain or wake drain) delivers that channel's whole tail, including threads addressed to other seats.

LIVE EVIDENCE (governor-e6b40560, chat_wait channels ["#governors","#general"]):
- Trigger: mention-less system lines in #workers, the file-collision notices msg-f9df6a37 (17:26:17Z) and msg-3f3261f9 (18:14:48Z). These route to every busy seat (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/chatStore.ts:228, unread at :247), the governor included.
- The 18:14Z wake then returned 7 #workers messages. 6 were addressed to other seats: msg-95448c0a and msg-4212ed1d mention worker-26483323/qa-7328a40d and worker-d6c1cb7a/qa-7328a40d; msg-ad0a356c and msg-eaeef84f are QA replies to those workers; msg-e841d20d and msg-3d887c9d are a worker's acks with no mentions.
- The 17:26Z wake likewise returned three 16:25Z worker acks (msg-2b4bea99, msg-23f5966d, msg-d6485b61) next to the routed msg-f9df6a37.
- The tool contract (chatWait.ts:371) promises "Optional ambient channel filter ... Routed mentions still arrive from any channel", i.e. only the routed ones.

IMPACT: every seat that gets one routed line in a busy channel such as #workers receives that channel's chatter. Notification-only worker sessions then "acknowledge" threads that were never theirs (e.g. msg-2b4bea99), adding to the collision/ack churn the governor measured on 11-02 (56 collision notices, 349 pages and 133 threaded acks in 3h). Related, already DONE: 48edc21b (deregistration presence lines defeating the filter) and 06cf7baf (which added unread channels to the drain).

FIX DIRECTION (the planner decides): make the drain apply the live path's relevance to every channel the caller doesn't watch (and to all channels when there is no filter). Deliver a message there only if it is routed to the caller: its raw mentions name the caller or a group token that resolves to it, a human sent it, or it is a mention-less system line (which routes to busy seats). Skipped messages still advance that channel's cursor and clear its unread, so they are never re-delivered later. Watched channels keep returning everything. Optional, as a separate call: whether mention-less #workers system lines should route to governor seats at all.
definitionOfDone: With a channels filter, chat_wait's backlog drains (entry and wake) deliver from an unwatched channel only messages routed to the caller, the same relevance isRelevant applies to live events. With no filter, the same holds for every scanned channel. Skipped messages advance that channel's cursor and are not delivered by a later call.

A vitest reproduces the defect: a caller watching #governors, a #workers message mentioning another seat, then a mention-less system line in #workers. The caller's chat_wait returns the system line but not the other seat's message. It fails on c99801aa (RED evidence in a task comment) and passes with the fix.

The existing chat_wait and chatBacklog tests stay green, including the routed-mention-outside-watched-channels case (06cf7baf), the registration floor (5902a670) and the sinceId cases (8b0b3edc). The vitest command and its result are in the completion evidence.

implementationPlan.description:
Add drain relevance and skip cursors to packages/moe-daemon/src/util/chatBacklog.ts. Use the session's own editing tool; Serena symbol editors fit this file. No shell writes.

1) Export chatWaitAdmits(channelSet: Set<string> | null, message: ChatMessage, routedToCaller: boolean): boolean. It is the one relevance rule:
- with a filter: channelSet.has(message.channel) || routedToCaller;
- with no filter: routedToCaller || message.sender === 'human'.

2) Add a non-exported routedToCaller(state, workerId). It returns a per-drain predicate over a STORED line; stored lines keep raw mentions, never routingTargets.
- When message.mentions is non-empty, resolve it with state.mentionRouter.parseMentions(message.content, ids, workers, teams). Build ids, workers and teams once per drain from Array.from(state.workers.values()) and Array.from(state.teams.values()). This is the router's own parser: code spans stripped, group tokens only in the addressing prefix, groups resolved by team role with the id-substring fallback. Never use the raw stored tokens (mem:gotcha-chat-group-token-line-start-and-two-parsers). If the parse names anyone, the line is routed only when it names workerId.
- If the line names nobody, it is routed only when the sender is 'system' or 'human'. The router broadcasts those to busy seats. An agent line addressed to nobody routes nowhere, and a departed seat's line must not pass as human.
- Never call MentionRouter.route() here: it changes hop counts and pauses.
- Comment the known over-deliveries. Each of these counts as routed, and none of them loses a routed line: a line in a paused (loop-guarded) channel, a line sent while the caller was not busy, and a parseMentions:false daemon echo (releaseTask's #workers copy).

3) BurstScope and ChatBurst gain two optional maps:
- skipAfter: Map<deliverable id, the last skipped id after it and before the channel's next deliverable line>;
- skipLead: Map<channelId, the last skipped id before the channel's first deliverable line, or its last skipped id when there is none>.
summarizeChatBurst sets a delivered scanned line's cursor to skipAfter.get(id) ?? id. It then gives each scanned channel that got no cursor its skipLead entry, and returns both maps on the burst so the entry and wake merge keeps them. A channel's delivered scanned lines are always a prefix: the caps keep the oldest slice, and the sort stays the stable, timestamp-only sort. So no cursor passes a deliverable line the caps dropped. fullyDrained keeps its rule, so a skip-only channel that was read to its end clears its unread.

4) collectChatBacklog (:153-205):
- Per channel, keep the own-post exclusion and the registration floor. Both stay transparent: they neither deliver nor move a cursor.
- Every other line is delivered when chatWaitAdmits(channelSet, line, isRouted(line)) holds. Otherwise it is recorded as skipped, for the two maps. Watched channels therefore return everything, as before.
- Paging: a filtered channel (no filter, or not in channelSet) that returns a full page with nothing deliverable reads on from that page's last id. The cap is a new exported MAX_SKIP_PAGES = 10 pages per channel per drain; the bound matters because each getMessages call re-reads up to 1 MB.
- A page with something deliverable, a watched channel, or the page cap stops the scan as today. Mark the channel partial when its last page was full.
- Error handling: the per-channel try/catch stays. A page that throws mid-channel is logged, leaves that channel's pending skipped run unrecorded (its cursor stays put), and never fails the tool.

5) Rewrite the doc comments that state the old behaviour: :144-152 ('No mention/human relevance filter is applied') and the backlogChannelIds note at :131-133.
implementationPlan.note:
chatBacklog.ts changes:
- Added the exported chatWaitAdmits and MAX_SKIP_PAGES=10, the private routedToCaller (MentionRouter.parseMentions over the current roster), and the optional skipAfter/skipLead maps via an exported SkipCursors that BurstScope and ChatBurst extend.
- summarizeChatBurst derives the skip cursors.
- collectChatBacklog now calls a scanChannel helper: relevance, skip-run paging, own-post and floor lines transparent, a throw records nothing for that channel.
- Doc comments rewritten.
Extra beyond the plan text, within the 'summarizeChatBurst cursor derivation' scope: if the caps drop an off-bus line that the scan never read, that channel keeps its plain cursor and ignores skip cursors. Such a line may be one the drain skipped while the live wake admitted it (e.g. an unknown sender), so this keeps the invariant that a cursor never passes the off-bus trigger.

implementationPlan.description:
Wire the shared rule and the skip cursors through packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatWait.ts, using the session's own editing tool.

(1) isRelevant (:169-184) keeps the #general feed check, its routingTargets source, and its refusal of the caller's own post when a filter is set. It returns chatWaitAdmits(this.ctx.channelSet, message, targets.includes(this.ctx.workerId)). The live path's behaviour does not change.

(2) Pass the skip maps into the merge:
- wake() (:258-263) passes drained itself as the merge scope;
- drainOnEntry (:297-300) passes drained ?? { partialChannels: new Set(), scannedChannels: new Set() }.
The final burst then keeps skipAfter and skipLead.

(3) drainOnEntry handles a skip-only scan: the drain found nothing to deliver, nothing is buffered, and drained.cursorUpdates is non-empty. In that case it awaits applyChatDelivery(state, workerId, drained) BEFORE this.entryDrainDone = true (:288), then returns if this.finished. The order matters. Events that arrive during that await are only buffered, so no wake can write a cursor at the same time. A buffered event then ships through the existing path with the same skip cursors, which rewrites them idempotently. Error handling: applyChatDelivery already logs its own failures and never throws, so the session still blocks or delivers.

Leave the tool description and the inputSchema text unchanged: its line 'Routed mentions still arrive from any channel' becomes true.

comments.author: architect-74d9e1c7
comments.content:
Architect decision on DoD 1 vs DoD 3, recorded before the plan:

DoD 1 requires the no-filter drain to apply the live relevance rule. Two existing no-filter rows in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/chatWait.test.ts assert the opposite, whole-tail delivery:
- 'returns every message that arrived, not just the one that woke the waiter' (:252). Its unrouted worker-peer chatter is exactly what DoD 1 now skips.
- 'does not advance a partially scanned channel past what the scan read (wake path)' (:364). Its unrouted worker-peer fillers would now be skipped.

The plan adapts these two rows rather than keeping them green as written:
- :252 becomes the no-filter wake regression: it returns the trigger only, the cursor lands on the trigger, and a follow-up wait times out.
- :364 posts its fillers as 'human', which the no-filter rule admits. Every assertion stays, so it still pins the partial-scan cursor.

The protections DoD 3 names keep their rows unchanged: routed mentions outside watched channels (06cf7baf), the registration floor (5902a670) and sinceId (8b0b3edc).

Prototype check in a scratch snapshot of c99801aa:
- With the fix, the full daemon suite passes: 244 files, 7096 passed, 24 skipped.
- The planned new rows and the adapted :252 fail on the c99801aa source. Every other row passes.

Two parts of the design were added because without them the fix would cause regressions:
- A filtered channel reads past full pages of skipped lines, up to 10 pages per drain.
- A skip-only entry drain writes its cursor and unread bookkeeping before it blocks.
Without these, a routed line behind 50 skipped lines in an unwatched channel would stall until a timeout.

comments.author: worker-8cf0816c
comments.content:
Adversarial self-review (step 6), for QA. The diff covers chatBacklog.ts +168/-40, chatWait.ts +25/-21, chatWait.test.ts +132/-7 and docs/MCP_SERVER.md +5/-5. It found no defect, so no fix and no gate re-run were needed. The step-5 gate passed on the final bytes: exit 0; chat files 121/121; full suite 247 files, 7117 passed, 24 skipped.

Changed existing rows:
- :252 asserted the no-filter whole-tail delivery that DoD 1 removes. It now asserts the reverse: only [trigger] is delivered, the #general cursor lands on the trigger, and a follow-up wait({}) times out. It is renamed 'skips unrouted chatter on a no-filter wake and delivers only the routed trigger'.
- :364 (wake path, partial scan) changed only its fillers' sender, to 'human' (the post() default, which the no-filter rule admits). Every assertion is unchanged, so it still pins the partial-scan cursor.
- The protections DoD 3 names are untouched and pass: routed mentions outside watched channels (06cf7baf, entry and wake, direct and role), the registration floor (5902a670) and sinceId (8b0b3edc).
- One row beyond the plan: unit row (g), 'keeps the plain cursor in a channel whose off-bus line the response budget dropped'. It covers a guard I added to summarizeChatBurst. If the caps drop an off-bus line the scan never read, that channel ignores skip cursors and keeps the plain cursor, because the dropped line may be one the drain skipped while the live wake admitted it. Mutants: removing the guard fails (g); MAX_SKIP_PAGES=1 fails (d); removing skipAfter fails (a) and (f); removing the entry bookkeeping fails (e); counting an agent line that names nobody as routed fails 5 rows.

(1) Parity, sender × address: drain = chatWaitAdmits + the stored-line rule; live = route() + isRelevant. They agree except in the three documented over-deliveries:
- a line in a paused channel;
- a mention-less system or human line sent while the caller was idle;
- a parseMentions:false echo.
Further divergences, none of which loses a routed line:
- Group membership changing between send and drain: the drain parses against the current roster and teams.
- Unknown senders: the router treats one as human, the drain does not. Unreachable at send time: chat_send refuses an unregistered workerId and addComment relays only registered authors. A later-departed seat's line was routed live as an agent line and is judged the same way by the drain.

(2) Cursors:
- Caps keep the oldest slice under the stable timestamp sort, so a channel's delivered scanned lines are a prefix of its deliverable ones. skipAfter of the last delivered line, and skipLead, both stop before the next deliverable line.
- A partial page only moves within what was read.
- An off-bus trigger never sets a cursor, and with the new guard a dropped one blocks skip cursors in its channel.
- A page read that throws records nothing for that channel.
- Out-of-order appends (timestamp taken before the channel mutex) are a pre-existing edge, unchanged.

(3) Concurrency:
- The entry skip write runs before entryDrainDone, so events arriving meanwhile only buffer. A buffered event then ships with the same skip cursors (an idempotent rewrite) and does not move a cursor itself.
- finished is checked before the write and after it. A cancel or timeout during the write only moves cursors over lines already judged skips.
- Two sessions of one worker with different filters can race one skip write against the other session's capped delivery. The window is tiny, and the same worker would have to switch filters mid-wait.

(4) Inputs:
- channels: [] is a filter that watches nothing, so only routed lines are delivered. The PowerShell pre-flight drain relies on this, and the registration-floor row covers it.
- An explicit sinceId in a filtered channel delivers routed lines from that point.
- An unregistered caller has no floor and no cursors; it gets mention-less system/human lines only if a scan runs, and the cursor write fails and is logged, as before.
- After a 10-page skip run the channel stays partial and unread, its cursor sits on page 10's last line, and the next call continues.
- An empty page breaks the loop.
- A no-cursor channel whose newest window is all skips reads one extra page, which is empty.

(5) Cost: extra pages are read only for a filtered channel whose raw page is full and holds nothing deliverable. Skip cursors then move past that chatter, so later drains of the channel are cheaper than before.

Size: chatBacklog.ts is now 369 lines, over the 300 soft cap; the plan pins all drain logic to this file.

acceptanceCriteria: Caller busy, watching #governors. In #workers: a line addressed to another seat, then a mention-less system line, then another seat's reply. Entry and wake drains return only the system line, the #workers cursor lands on the reply, unread is cleared, and the next call times out.
With no filter, the same drain returns the system line plus any human line, never a seat-to-seat line that does not route to the caller.
A skip-only entry drain (no filter, explicit sinceId, nothing routed) times out with the channel's cursor on its last skipped line.
A routed line behind more than PER_CHANNEL_SCAN_LIMIT skipped lines in a filtered channel is delivered by one call.

The existing rows for routed mentions outside watched channels (06cf7baf), the registration floor (5902a670) and sinceId (8b0b3edc) pass unchanged. Only the two no-filter rows that asserted whole-tail delivery are adapted, and a task comment documents the change.
invariants: A cursor never advances past a deliverable line that was not delivered (burst count cap, response budget, partial page, off-bus trigger).
Off-bus messages (the wake trigger, buffered events) never move a cursor.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Storing routingTargets, or an echo flag, on each message so the drain could replay the exact live decision. Rejected: it changes the stored message schema and grows every broadcast line in the 1 MB tail window. The reconstruction errs only toward over-delivery. (2) Filtering only unwatched channels under a filter and leaving the no-filter path alone. Rejected: DoD 1 requires the no-filter path too. (3) Calling MentionRouter.route() from the drain. Rejected: it changes hop counts and clears pauses on human lines. (4) Skipping without paging. Rejected: a routed line behind 50 skipped ones in an unwatched channel would stall, because the entry drain finds nothing deliverable and blocks until the timeout. That would be a regression from today's 50-per-call whole-tail delivery. Paging plus the entry skip bookkeeping guarantee progress. (5) Not done, a separate call per the task: whether mention-less #workers system lines should route to governor seats at all.

planningNotes.risks: The entry skip bookkeeping must run before entryDrainDone. Otherwise a concurrent wake's cursor write can be overtaken by the older skip position, which only duplicates a delivery but is avoidable. Keep the stable timestamp-only sort (mem:gotcha-chat-wait-burst-drain). The RED test file must import only symbols c99801aa has. Never resolve groups from raw stored tokens: parseRawMentions ignores the addressing-prefix rule, so a mid-prose group tag would over-deliver. Accepted, documented over-deliveries: an addressed line in a loop-guarded channel, a mention-less system or human line sent while the caller was idle, and a parseMentions:false daemon echo in #workers. The DoD 3 wording conflicts with DoD 1 for two existing rows; the architect comment on the task records the decision.

completionSummary:

Outside the caller's channels filter, and in every scanned channel when there is no filter, they deliver only lines routed to the caller, plus any human line when there is no filter.
